brief: Goldman's Industrials & Materials desk opens with hedge funds reversing five weeks of US Industrials selling into the fastest net buying since early January (+1.8 SDs), concentrated in Aerospace & Defense, Construction & Engineering, Airlines and Industrial Conglomerates, even as the long/short ratio stays low (15th percentile 1-year). Into Q3 earnings, GS likes HII, WWD, TDG, ARXS, AVEX and is cautious on LMT, BAH, MRCY; expects strong aerospace aftermarket results on priced-in negativity, Boeing 737 MAX and 787 output still behind plan, and large-cap defense wrestling with peak DoD budget authorization risk. FAST (6% implied move, four straight post-earnings declines, consensus EBIT seen too high) and JBHT (stock down to $230 from $270-280 on a flagged EPS miss, but short interest halved) report this week. Chemicals: Q3 shaping up weaker than consensus as Middle East supply curtailment proved less bullish than expected; PE pricing has fallen but September may rise 3-5c/lb; PVC set to decline 2-4% in Q4 before a 2027 rebound. Housing: GS cuts 2026 single-family starts to 900k (-4.6% YOY) on higher mortgage rates, raises R&R forecasts on pricing, but sees seasonality and depressed valuations (52% near 52-week lows) as upside risk, favoring AWI, CSL, FBIN, IBP.
